A slot machine for taking photographs. Quite a few of these machines may be found in public places in New York City. The person wishing to be photographed takes the position they think the most charming, then a deposit of ten cents into the slot, the arc light is turned on for a few seconds and as soon as the exposure is finished the light is shut off. It is possible to hear the machinery working inside. Within a minute a and a half the finished photograph falls into a up on the left side of the machine. It has proven to a great money maker.
NEW MECHANICAL AIR CAMERA.

A new Air Camera is on view today at the Air Ministry which is the latest in Aerial photography. It is worked by electricity and operated and controlled from a switchboard. This camera is to be used in all expeditions. O.P.S. Mr. Colin M. Williamson photographed this morning with the camera, which is set in the model of a cockpit of an aeroplane. FI.

A camera for the photographing of explosive gases has been invented in Chicago by A.H.Nuckolls of the Chicago Underwriters Laboratories. Mr.Nuckolls has been working on the camera over a period of five years at a cost of $10,000. Photo shows the inventor adjusting one of the lenses. The ten foot pipe in the foreground is used to explode the gases while they are being photo-stra phed. The pipe has seven perisoscopic lenses leading to the camera. On the left is the camera showing the inside drum to hold a roll of film. The drum travels at a speed of ten thousand feet per second. 3/17/23

This picture was made by a film camera man who snapped two of his friends in a lonely canyon nearLos Angeles two months ago. Recently he developed itand noticed the face and breast of a woman at the bottom of the picture, that can be seen in the picture, though he saw nothing but his friends when Hez made the photo.
